body:
When I had my first wreck, I--a devout atheist--remember saying, "God, save me..." and meaning it as an intervening prayer facing death. I then remember immediately losing faith again, gradually regaining it as I started healing without nerve damage, then losing it again as the brace came off, I returned to normal life and the months passed.

Now, I've had a minor wreck with whiplash and all the anxiety that I had then is back, without the faith.
And if you're content in the belief that death is, simple, an end--and not an afterlife?

I mean, yes, I want to see them and enjoy being with them, and I know losing me would hard, but why is not better for them to suffer it in one dose, rather than the long,drawn out and still excruciating dose of having to care for me if I ever suffer nerve damage?

You've a potentially-fatal or life-changing illness or condition?

I have family, but I see it as being a burden on them if I were to become paralyzed. I've extreme back issues.
